label: Miami University Art Museum Mandaic bowl (Yamauchi 2000)
summary: Mandaic healing and protection bowl for Sisinayid son of Zad-Anosh and his household, re-edited by Ohad Abudraham from published photographs and a Schøyen parallel.

appearance.locator: pp. 13–30; Miami University Art Museum bowl
appearance.description: Complete new edition of the Miami University Art Museum Mandaic bowl originally published by Edwin Yamauchi in 2000.
appearance.rationale: The article explicitly identifies and re-edits one bowl in the Miami University Art Museum.

identifiers.notes: The English summary calls the object the Miami Bowl; no museum accession number appears in the article.

claims.notes: The source says width rather than explicitly stating diameter.

claims.value_text: Eleven physical lines, with the final line on the exterior
claims.notes: The bowl description says eleven lines, while the printed transcription and translation are numbered 1–10. This internal discrepancy is retained for later image-level checking rather than adjudicated.

claims.value_text: Composed of seven differently sized fragments that join almost perfectly with little damage to the inscription; text generally well preserved
Spiral from the centre to the upper rim, ending in one exterior line; small and large circular rulings define the inner blank and outer boundary
Cursive Mandaic hand, somewhat careless, in broad prominent ink
Sisinayid son of Zad-Anosh, his spouse, sons, and daughters
claims.notes: The source discusses the uncertain reading history of the Iranian personal names. This transliteration follows Abudraham's Hebrew presentation and is not an independent reading.

claims.value_text: Healing, arming, sealing, and protection for the client, his family, house, dwelling, building, food, water, and probably livestock
The ʿAlmay dēw and the paired nālē and nʿūlē demons
claims.notes: Abudraham discusses these beings as afflicting or attaching themselves to attractive men and women and compares traditions associating them with incubus, asthma, and migraine.

claims.value_text: Schøyen MS 2054/47, lines 4–8, supplies a close unpublished parallel used in the new reading
Abudraham argues that Hilprecht 40c (VT 1981.8) was written by the same hand
claims.notes: Source-attributed paleographic proposal based on script shape, letter size, layout, and a similarly read beneficiary name; no object identity merge or independent scribal adjudication is made.

claims.value_text: Abudraham supplies a new transcription, translation, and commentary correcting numerous readings in Yamauchi's 2000 edition

label: Hilprecht Collection VT 1981.8 / bowl 40c
summary: Mandaic Hilprecht Collection bowl used by Abudraham as a close paleographic and beneficiary-name comparandum for the Miami bowl.

appearance.description: Comparative discussion of Hilprecht bowl 40c / VT 1981.8; this article does not re-edit the object.
appearance.rationale: The source explicitly identifies the separate Hilprecht bowl by two designations and compares it with the Miami bowl.

claims.notes: Abudraham offers an independent reading and notes substantial similarity to the Miami beneficiary name; Müller-Kessler's published reading differs.

claims.value_text: Abudraham argues that VT 1981.8 and the Miami bowl were written by the same hand
claims.notes: Source-attributed paleographic proposal based on script shape, letter size, and layout. The records remain distinct and no authorship judgment is made by the index.

claims.value_text: Published as bowl 40c by Müller-Kessler; cited as a comparandum rather than re-edited by Abudraham
